card.title: 40. PANZERGRENADIER
card.text: Deployment: Send a unit to hand. Draw a card if it is friendly.
card.flavorText: The 40th Panzergrenadier Regiment was a key infantry component of the 17th Panzer Division, created from Schützen-Regiment 40 in 1942. It was structured to fight alongside tanks, providing mobile infantry support in fast-moving operations. The regiment was active from the division’s early campaigns on the Eastern Front through to the final months of the war. In 1941, the 17th Panzer Division launched its offensive with Army Group South during Operation Barbarossa, pushing into Ukraine and capturing key cities like Smolensk and Bryansk. The 40th Regiment took part in these rapid advances, often engaging Soviet forces in fierce encounters around river crossings and fortified positions. In 1942, the regiment fought near Stalingrad as the division attempted to relieve the 6th Army. Though it avoided encirclement, it suffered significant losses. Throughout 1943 and 1944, the 40th Panzergrenadier Regiment was heavily engaged in defensive actions across southern Russia and later in Poland. It was continuously weakened by Soviet offensives and shortages of equipment. By 1945, the regiment had been reduced to scattered remnants as the division retreated into Czechoslovakia, where it surrendered in May.
